source.title: Data Value in the Age of Scaling: Understanding LLM Scaling Dynamics Under Real-Synthetic Data Mixtures
source.authors: Hao-Hui Wang; Jingyuan Qi; Jian-Peng Chen; Jun Wu; Lifu Huang; Lecheng Zheng; Kevin Choi; Balaji Veeramani; Edward Bowen; Alison Hu; Tyler Cody; Da-Wei Zhou

record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper derives and empirically examines a three-phase loss-scaling pattern under real–synthetic data mixtures, refining how scaling behavior should be described in that setting.
record.gate_note: The paper tests loss as training sample size increases, not scaling with parameter count or compute. Its empirical scaling test is on CIFAR-100 with ResNet-18; a separate simulation varies the real-data mixture ratio. Data-valuation correlations, runtime results, and cited scaling-law findings are not rows because they do not measure the scaling behavior at issue.
record.test_reason: The paper derives and argues for a three-phase, non-single-power-law loss curve versus training sample size under long-tail real–synthetic mixtures. It checks this on ResNet-18/CIFAR-100 (figure only). Its LLM experiments test only data valuation, not scaling.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors claim a three-phase scaling pattern with breakpoints at k^β and k^β/π under real–synthetic mixtures, shown empirically only for ResNet-18 on CIFAR-100. Their main further conclusion is that a generalization bound yields a data-valuation score that correlates better with ground truth than baselines, at low cost.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies training-sample-size scaling under long-tail real–synthetic mixtures, including an image-classification experiment and a theoretical model. It does not reproduce parameter-, token-, or compute-scaling sweeps from the original sources.
record.method_sensitivity: The analyzed behavior depends on the real-data proportion π and tail cutoff k; the empirical image experiment uses π = 0.0625 and k = 70, while the simulation varies π from 0 to 1.
record.problems: The empirical scaling test is limited to one image-classification backbone and a constructed long-tail real–synthetic dataset. The plotted loss values are not numerically reported in the text, and the study does not fit or compare power laws.
record.rows_left_out: Data-valuation correlation, runtime, and subsampling-stability results were left out because they do not measure the scaling behavior in the claim. No additional scaling-loss results are reported in the provided text.

untested.parts: Video, repeated data, fine-tuning and transfer were not tested. Image classification was tested only under a constructed long-tail real/corrupted mixture, with no fitted exponent.
Parameter counting, training schedule and fitting method were not varied. No exponents or compute-optimal splits were estimated. Only data-composition dependence was examined.
Not tested: there is no language-model pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens or compute.
Not tested: the Qwen/Llama experiments measure data-valuation correlation, not scaling.

missing.what: Accuracy versus training size (overall, head, tail) with predicted breakpoints, which is the companion to the loss rows

record.verdict_notes: Despite the 'LLM scaling' title, the only empirical scaling evidence is one image classifier on a constructed long tail, reported as figures without fitted exponents or numbers. R5 is a simulation of the authors' own formula and should not count as evidence. The data-valuation tables are correctly excluded.

versions.untested_parts: Language-model held-out pretraining loss scaling with parameters, tokens, or compute.
Whether fits from small runs predict much larger runs.
Compute-optimal parameter and token allocation as compute changes.
Effects of depth, width, and other architecture choices at fixed parameter count.
The study examines image classification with a real–synthetic mixture, but not video, repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer, and it does not fit or compare power-law forms.
Predictability of downstream task performance from scale or pretraining loss.
The study does not vary parameter-count conventions, training schedules, or fitting methods, and does not estimate or compare scaling exponents or compute-optimal splits.

rows.subject: knowledge-frequency model (Lemma 1)
rows.operation_detail: Derives test-error scaling as training sample size grows for a long-tail knowledge distribution with a truncated synthetic-data tail.
rows.measure: Test error versus training sample size
rows.value: Three regimes: rapid learning for |S| ≤ c1 k^β; a plateau for c1 k^β < |S| < c2 k^β/π; and tail learning for |S| ≥ c2 k^β/π. The stated breakpoints are |S| = k^β and |S| = k^β/π.
rows.note: The result is an analysis under the lemma's stated distribution and learning assumptions, not a fit to language-model pretraining runs.
rows.check: Analytic result under the paper's own assumptions, not a measurement. It is a specific argument that the curve bends (a plateau between power-law-like phases) depending on the data mix. It does not bear on V5, which concerns empirical form in other regimes.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Varies total training sample size and evaluates test loss on a balanced CIFAR-100 test set.

conditions.value: CIFAR-100 real data and CIFAR-100-C synthetic data

rows.measure: Test loss versus training sample size
rows.value: The text reports that overall loss reduction slows in the plateau phase; plotted values are figure only.
rows.note: The paper describes an overall three-phase pattern but gives no numerical loss values in the text.
rows.check: Figure-only, with no power-law fit and no numbers. The text says loss falls, then plateaus, then falls again. For V5 this is a power-law-like decline interrupted by a plateau, so partial. For V7 the bend is reported as observed in words. Breakpoint agreement is not quantified.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Varies total training sample size and evaluates test loss on a balanced CIFAR-100 test set.

conditions.value: CIFAR-100 real data and CIFAR-100-C synthetic data

rows.measure: Head-class test loss versus training sample size
rows.value: The text reports a sharp decrease in head-class loss during rapid learning; plotted values are figure only.
rows.note: The paper attributes the early loss reduction to learning head knowledge from both real and synthetic data.
rows.check: Head-class loss only. It bears on the mechanism of the first breakpoint, not on whether overall loss follows a power law, so V5 is removed. Figure-only.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Varies total training sample size and evaluates test loss on a balanced CIFAR-100 test set.

conditions.value: CIFAR-100 real data and CIFAR-100-C synthetic data

rows.measure: Tail-class test loss versus training sample size
rows.value: The text reports that tail-class loss drops rapidly in the tail-learning phase as real tail samples accumulate; plotted values are figure only.
rows.note: The study reports this result alongside improvement in tail-class accuracy.
rows.check: Tail-class loss only. It bears on the second-phase drop, not on overall power-law form, so V5 is removed. Figure-only.

rows.subject: three-phase scaling simulation
rows.operation_detail: Simulates test-loss scaling with training sample size at different real–synthetic mixture ratios.
rows.measure: Simulated test error versus training sample size
rows.value: The text says the three-phase behavior holds consistently across the different mixture ratios; plotted values are figure only.
rows.note: This is a simulation, not an additional empirical language-model training sweep.
rows.check: Numerical evaluation of the paper's own analytic model (assumed ρ, γ), not a trained system. It shows the lemma's behaviour, not evidence about real models.

relationships.condition: ResNet-18 on CIFAR-100 with a p_i∝i^-2 long tail, synthetic data truncated at k=70 (π=0.0625), scaling with sample size
relationships.reason: The text reports overall loss plateauing between head- and tail-learning drops: a bend driven by data composition (R2–R4, figure-only; theory R1).
relationships.display_finding: Overall loss plateaus between improvements from learning frequent and rare classes, producing a bend driven by data composition.

relationships.condition: Image classification trained on long-tail real data mixed with tail-truncated synthetic data
relationships.reason: Loss versus sample size shows a mid-range plateau rather than one smooth power law. Stated in text, no fit or numbers (R2).
relationships.display_finding: Loss plateaued at intermediate sample sizes rather than following one smooth power law.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: CIFAR-100 image classification with a long-tail class distribution and real–synthetic data mixtures
reader_labels.reason: The reported image-task loss behavior has rapid-learning, plateau, and tail-learning phases; the study does not establish that one power-law form applies in this setting (R1–R5).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Long-tail real–synthetic mixtures in the stated analysis, CIFAR-100 experiment, and mixture-ratio simulation
reader_labels.reason: The study reports a three-phase loss pattern with breakpoints, including a plateau and later tail-learning gains, rather than a single uniform scaling regime (R1–R5).
